GITHUB ACTIONS – CI/CD WORKFLOW

HOW AM I DEPLOYING MY APPLICATION?

3 main operations:

1 . Updating the Docker image 
→ Jib builds a new Docker image and pushes it to Docker Hub with a new tag (Git commit SHA). 
→ It also pushes the latest tag.

2 . Updating the respective Deployment's image in GKE 
→  kubectl set image  updates the container's image reference in the GKE Deployment.

3 . Replacing the Pods 
→ Kubernetes performs a rolling update. 
→ It gradually creates new Pods using the updated image and terminates the old Pods. 
→ We don't manually restart each Pod.

4 MAIN PARTS OF A GITHUB ACTIONS WORKFLOW

1. name
2. on
3. env
4. jobs

1 . name

→ Name of the workflow.

2 . on

→ Specifies when the workflow should be triggered.

Example: 
→ When code is pushed to the master branch. 
→ When changes happen in specified directories/files.

3 . env

→ Constant/reusable values that we define once and use throughout the workflow.

Example: 
SERVICE_NAME: account-service 
IMAGE_NAME: nishanthtalari/lovable-account-service

4 . jobs

1. Each job gets its own VM (runner) from GitHub servers.
2. We specify which OS/environment we want using  runs-on:  inside the job. 
   Example:  runs-on: ubuntu-latest 
3. Each job contains multiple steps.
4. Each step can have its own  name .
5. Steps inside the same job execute sequentially.

INSIDE EACH STEP

We generally use either:

A.  uses:  + optional  with: 

uses: 
→ Specifies an existing GitHub Action that should be executed on the runner. 
→ Example:  actions/setup-java@v4  sets up Java on the runner.

with: 
→ Passes inputs/configuration to the action specified using  uses: . 
→ Example: Specifying the Java version and distribution.

B.  run:  + optional  working-directory: 

Used when we want to execute our own/custom shell commands.

working-directory: 
→ Specifies the directory from which commands should execute. 
→ Can be a relative or absolute path.

run: | 
→ Used to write multiple lines of shell commands. 
→ The pipe ( | ) allows us to write commands on separate lines.

Example:

working-directory: ./account-service 
run: | 
command1
command2
command3

IMPORTANT: 
→ We don't need   \  at the end of every command.
→ Use    \ only when continuing the SAME command across multiple lines.

Example:

run: | 
command1  
argument1  
argument2

IN SHORT:

 uses:  + optional  with:  
→ Execute an existing GitHub Action with the required inputs.

 run:  + optional  working-directory:  
→ Execute our own shell commands.

NAME INSIDE JOBS / STEPS

 name:  → A descriptive name. We can give it any meaningful name.

→  name  can be used at workflow, job and step levels. 
→ It is optional for individual jobs and steps.

PASSING SECRET VALUES

1 . Add secret values in GitHub:

Repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions.

2 . Access them inside the workflow using:

 ${{ secrets.YOUR_SECRET_NAME }} 

For non-sensitive reusable values, we can use GitHub Variables:

 ${{ vars.YOUR_VARIABLE_NAME }} 

COMPLETE CI/CD FLOW

Git push 
↓ 
GitHub Actions workflow gets triggered 
↓ 
GitHub Actions runner (VM) 
↓ 
Checkout code 
↓ 
Set up JDK 
↓ 
Build and install Common Library 
↓ 
Build Account Service using Jib 
↓ 
Jib builds and pushes the Docker image to Docker Hub 
↓ 
Authenticate with GCP 
↓ 
Get GKE cluster credentials 
↓ 
 kubectl set image  updates the Deployment 
↓ 
Kubernetes performs a rolling update 
↓ 
Old Pods are gradually replaced by new Pods 
↓ 
 kubectl rollout status  confirms whether the rollout is complete.
